cves.description: A vulnerability was detected in TRENDnet TEW-751DR 1.03B01. Affected by this vulnerability is the function gena.php::GENA_notify_init of the file htdocs/upnpinc/gena.php of the component UPnP Event Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument uri results in os command injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.

A security vulnerability has been detected in TRENDnet TEW-751DR and TEW-733GR 1.03B01. Affected is the function soapcgi_main of the file /soap.cgi of the component UPnP Igd Control Endpoint. Such manipulation of the argument service leads to os command injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

Budibase Server from 3.39.18 before 4.0.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to erase MongoDB query filters by supplying __proto__ as a dynamic JSON key in PUBLIC queries. Attackers can send a single request to the query execution endpoint, reducing the filter to {} to read, update, or delete every document in the collection.

A vulnerability was found in D-Link R32 1.10B02. This affects an unknown function of the file /usr/bin/httpd of the component flupl self Endpoint. Performing a manipulation of the argument fpath results in os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

A security flaw has been discovered in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11_multi. The impacted element is the function formSetSafeWanWebMan of the file /goform/SetRemoteWebCfg. The manipulation of the argument remoteIp results in command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A vulnerability was identified in Netis WF2409E up to 20261026. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file /cgi-bin/skk_set.cgi of the component CGI Interface. The manipulation of the argument app/password/new_pwd_confirm/passwd_set/mode_name/wl_link leads to improper authentication. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in Volans NGFW Next-Generation Firewall r5.1. Impacted is the function exec of the file sslvpn/sslvpn_client.php of the component SSLVPN Client. Such manipulation of the argument img leads to os command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

Smart Portal developed by Direk Tech has a Missing Authorization vulnerability. Authenticated remote attackers can add a specified account to the Active Directory Domain Admins group, thereby obtaining domain administrator privileges.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a broken object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to reference other tenants' files by supplying arbitrary attachment keys on row save. Attackers can inject a victim app's attachment key into a row, then update or delete the row to delete that object from the shared APPS bucket or read it via presigned URLs.

A vulnerability has been found in D-Link R32 1.10B02. The impacted element is the function SetDeviceSettings of the file /usr/bin/httpd of the component DHMAPI Action Handler. Such manipulation of the argument TZLocation leads to os command injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

A vulnerability was determined in Volans NGFW Next-Generation Firewall r5.1. This issue affects the function exec/system of the file modules/assets/port_serve_scan.mds of the component Web Management UI. This manipulation of the argument task_name/where/path causes os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in Panabit Smart Application Gateway TANGr7p10. This vulnerability affects the function edit_data_pie of the file /cgi-bin/flowcontrol/ajax_data_pie. This manipulation of the argument Name causes os command injection. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

A vulnerability was found in D-Link DCS-935L 1.10.01. This affects the function loginRouter of the file web/cgi-bin/localrecording/setconf.cgi of the component Local Recording CGI. Performing a manipulation of the argument account/password results in os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a command injection vulnerability in its GitHub Actions release workflow, which interpolates the pull request title directly into a shell run block. Attackers can submit a pull request against a release branch with shell metacharacters in its title that, once merged, executes commands with a cross-repository GITHUB_TOKEN, enabling unauthorized merges into enterprise repositories.

The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy_files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy_files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.

The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. The handler sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content_callback() is registered on the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call_user_func() after only a function_exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.

Frappe Framework before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Document.update() that fails to validate whether the caller is permitted to submit or modify the target document. Attackers can invoke document update operations to submit or alter documents they are not authorized to change.

ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an authentication bypass in its server OAuth SSO sign-in module, which resolves Google and Git SSO logins solely by the provider-asserted email without checking email_verified or binding the SSO subject. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a trusted-issuer token carrying a victim's unverified email to the SSO callback to obtain the victim's session, including admin accounts.

Budibase from 3.41.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to take over password-less global Builder accounts via unverified-email OIDC/SSO account linking. Attackers can assert a victim's email with email_verified=false at a trusted IdP, bypassing the isAccountLinkable allowlist to control all apps, datasources, and automations.

The Product Input Fields for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0 via the process_file_input_field function. This is due to missing file type validation in the process_file_input_field function, which accepts the client-supplied multipart Content-Type header as the sole type gate and writes the uploaded file to the unprotected pif_temp directory using the verbatim client-supplied filename. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one product with a File-type Product Input Field with the "Show thumbnail" option enabled, which is a standard use of the feature; additionally, the pif_temp/ upload directory is created without .htaccess or index.php restrictions, leaving written files directly web-accessible and executable on default Apache/mod_php configurations.

llama.cpp b11450 before b12658 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ggml RPC server that allows unauthenticated attackers to write to arbitrary heap addresses via zero-element destination tensors. Attackers can learn buffer bases with BUFFER_GET_BASE, then send RPC_CMD_COPY_TENSOR with a destination pointer below the buffer base to crash the server or execute code.

Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability in Drupal Drupal core allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels. This issue affects Drupal core versions: from 0.0.0 to 10.6.22, from 11.0.0 to 11.3.22, from 11.4.0 to 11.4.13.

build-git-clone before 1.0.4 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the clone() function that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted repository URLs. Attackers can embed shell metacharacters such as ; or $() in the url argument, which is concatenated into a sh -c command, to execute operating system commands with Node.js process privileges.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the report module (openimis-be-report_py) where the /api/report/reportbro/preview endpoint evaluates printIf expressions server-side using simpleeval with an insufficient name-prefix blocklist. An attacker can craft an expression that reaches sys.modules['os'] via datetime.sys to execute arbitrary operating-system commands as root, and can also exploit the same endpoint's key parameter for unauthenticated arbitrary file read, enabling full host compromise including exposure of database credentials and JWT signing keys.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows SQL Injection.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

FFmpeg 4.4 before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_deband.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a runtime coupling command. Attackers can send a 'deband coupling 1' command via sendcmd or an unauthenticated zmq filter, making chroma planes be processed at luma dimensions to crash the process or potentially execute code.

Deserialization of untrusted data in double-submit cookie vs. form field validation in Idunno.AntiCsrf versions through 0.9.1 Beta on ASP.NET allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute code via object injection

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability that could result in privilege escalation. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to gain elevated access to sensitive data or functionality. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

compose-farm 0.19.0 before 1.22.0 contains a cross-site WebSocket hijacking and cross-site request forgery vulnerability because its unauthenticated web UI performs no Origin validation. Malicious websites visited by users can open /ws/shell/{host} or /ws/exec sockets, or abuse unquoted service parameters and PUT /api/console/file, to execute commands on all managed hosts.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') in Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authorization bypass because the sanitizePath entry point option leaves dot-segments carrying path parameters, such as /..;x/, unresolved when matching routers and applying middlewares. Unauthenticated attackers can send requests like /public/..;x/admin to a parameter-stripping backend shared with a protected router, bypassing authentication or authorization middlewares to reach protected resources.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in module.json providers and composer.json psr-4 namespace parsing that derives destination folder names without excluding traversal characters. Attackers with module.create permission can upload a crafted module ZIP to write PHP files into the public directory, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution.

The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.0 via deserialization of untrusted input . This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present. The incomplete remediation in version 7.2.0 applied escape_pdf_note() only to the customer_note path; the billing address path at woocommerce/shortcodes.php:975–978 remains unpatched, and exploitation requires guest checkout to be enabled along with a payment method that transitions orders to on-hold status (such as the stock WooCommerce Direct Bank Transfer option).

The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.2 This is due to a flaw in `WPJOBPORTALuser::__construct()` where the non-empty guard on the `wpjobportal-socialid` cookie is evaluated against the raw cookie value before `sanitize_key()` is applied — allowing a value composed entirely of characters outside `[a-z0-9_-]` to pass the guard, be reduced to an empty string by `sanitize_key()`, and be used as the literal value in a `WHERE socialid = ''` database query that matches the first portal account whose `socialid` column is empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to be bound to an existing WP Job Portal Employer or Jobseeker account, gaining the ability to create, edit, and delete the victim's companies, job listings, resumes, and applications, as well as overwrite the linked WordPress user's first name, last name, and display name via the `saveuser`→`syncWPUserName()` path. Exploitation is viable on virtually all installations because every portal account not registered through the social-login flow retains the default empty `socialid` value; nonce checks on downstream actions such as `savecompany` and `saveuser` do not mitigate this issue because those nonces are minted within the already-hijacked session and validate against the attacker's own subsequent requests. Successful exploitation gives the attacker control of a distinct, already-privileged WP Job Portal Employer / Jobseeker (bound to a specific WordPress user) account; it does not promote the attacker's original account.

The WordPress File Upload plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in versions up to, and including, 5.3.1 via the 'wfu_ajax_action_handshake' and 'wfu_ajax_action_send_email_notification' AJAX Actions. This is due to the unauthenticated handshake accepting a 'sid' parameter sanitized only with sanitize_text_field(), which does not strip '[', ']', '{', or '}', allowing the sid to be crafted as an item name containing embedded delimiter pairs that plant forged records for arbitrary other item names — including the per-session file path list and the consent flag — in the plugin's shared concatenated user-state option store, combined with the notification handler being gated only by a nonce freely minted by the same nopriv handshake. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.8.9 This is due to the site-wide signing secret `swpm_private_key_one` being generated at install time with PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid('', true)` function in `SwpmInstallation::installer()`, whose timestamp-derived keyspace (~10^15 candidates / ~50 bits) can be constrained via the public WordPress REST API date of the plugin's auto-created registration page, combined with a single-MD5 oracle (`md5(key|level)`) that the public registration form prints as `swpm_level_hash` and a non-constant-time `!=` comparison in `SwpmFrontRegistration::register_front_end()` as the sole authorization gate on which membership level a visitor may register into; `SwpmUtils::get_free_level()` then honors an attacker-posted `level_identifier=md5(level)` regardless of the configured free-membership setting, and `prepare_and_create_wp_user_front_end()` creates the WordPress account with whatever role the level is configured to grant (only the `administrator` role is refused). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers, after an offline brute-force recovery of the install-time secret against the public MD5 oracle, to forge a valid `swpm_level_hash` for any configured membership level and self-register into that level, elevating their newly created WordPress account to the level's assigned role — e. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete editor role.

A weakness has been identified in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11_multi. This affects the function fromAdvSetMacMtuWan of the file /goform/AdvSetMacMtuWan. This manipulation of the argument mac causes command injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

A security vulnerability has been detected in D-Link R95 101B06. Affected by this issue is the function GetBluetoothAdapterSettings/GetBluetoothBloodPressure/GetBluetoothDeviceList/GetBluetoothScanDeviceList/SetBluetoothAdapterSettings/SetBluetoothUnpairDevice/SetTriggerBluetoothScan/SetBluetoothPairDevice of the file /bin/ssi of the component DHMAPI SOAP Handler. The manipulation of the argument inner_xml leads to os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Password Recovery Exploitation.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

A weakness has been identified in TRENDnet TEW-751DR 1.03B01. This impacts the function FUN_0040ed90 of the file wfadev.cgi of the component UPnP/WFA. This manipulation of the argument SOAPAction causes stack-based buffer overflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. A high degree of complexity is needed for the attack. The exploitability is said to be difficult. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

Kestra before 1.3.36 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting HTML into the executions page sort parameter. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted link whose invalid sort value is rendered unsanitized in an error toast, stealing the non-HttpOnly BASIC_AUTH credential cookie to take over the instance.

D-Link DWM-222W developed by D-Link Corporation has a Use of Hard-coded Credentials vulnerability. Unauthenticated adjacent network attackers can use the administrator account embedded in the firmware to access the configuration backup endpoint and obtain plaintext passwords for all user accounts.

The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Warehouse Cargo theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in versions up to, and including, 2.7.4 via the warehouse_cargo_install_and_activate_plugin() AJAX handler. The handler is registered on wp_ajax_ but performs no nonce verification and no capability check, allowing any authenticated user to supply an attacker-controlled URL that the server fetches, writes into wp-content/plugins/ with file_put_contents(), extracts with unzip_file() (which does not filter file extensions), and then activates via activate_plugin(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to upload arbitrary files on the affected site's server which makes remote code execution possible.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a path traversal vulnerability in validateStackPath, which omits the isProtectedPath() check and permits writes to protected system directories. Authenticated users with stacks:edit permission can send a crafted composePath to PUT /api/stacks/[name]/compose to write arbitrary files, such as cron payloads, achieving remote code execution as root.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass in the internal database (TJDB) PostgREST proxy, which grants proxy access to every logged-in user and derives the database role and schema from the client-supplied tj-workspace-id header. Any authenticated workspace member can send requests to /api/tooljet-db/proxy/<tableId> to read and modify TJDB tables, bypassing app, query, and table permissions, and in SQL-mode-disabled (Cloud) deployments can access all tenants' tables.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass in instance-level Google SSO because the id_token audience is not verified when no Google OAuth client ID is configured, the shipped default. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a Google-signed id_token minted for their own OAuth client to /api/sso/sign-in/common/google without an organizationId, obtaining a session as any existing user with the matching email.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows workspace-scoped builders to access other workspaces' backups by supplying a foreign backupId. Attackers can substitute predictable backup IDs in backup download, import, update, or delete routes to steal archives, restore victim data into their workspace, or delete backups.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted subjects to execute arbitrary queries by calling the JavaScript surrealdb.query() bridge. Attackers permitted to run a specific script can bypass the Capabilities::allows_query() gate in the query module to execute unrestricted queries beyond their predefined operations.
Mail2000 developed by Openfind has an OS Command Injection vulnerability.Authenticated remote attackers can inject arbitrary OS commands and execute them on the server.
MailGates/MailAudit developed by Openfind has a Command Injection vulnerability.Authenticated remote attackers can inject commands and execute them on the server.

Grav Form plugin before 9.2.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows page authors to write uploads into Twig template folders by setting an unchecked file field destination in Form::uploadFiles(). Attackers can upload .txt or .svg files containing Twig and have them rendered as trusted templates outside the sandbox, executing code as the web server user.

Handesk through 1.5 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in Attachment::storeAttachmentFromRequest() that allows authenticated agents to upload files with arbitrary extensions by attaching them to ticket comments without extension, MIME type, or size validation. Attackers can upload a PHP file via POST /tickets/{ticket}/comments, which is stored under storage/app/public/attachments and served from /storage/attachments/, to achieve remote code execution as the web server user or serve malicious HTML/SVG content from the application origin.

Comviva Revenue Plus (MobiLytix Customer Value Management) 3.0.0 contains an expression language injection vulnerability in the user administration module, where the POST /rp/manageUser endpoint handled by manageUsersAction evaluates the name of an arbitrary request parameter as a server-side Java EL expression before rendering the response. The only protection is a denylist of reflective method names, which does not cover constructor-based access to a JDK scripting engine, so authenticated low-privilege attackers can supply an EL expression as a parameter name to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the application server account. This product is no longer supported by the vendor; standard support ended on 2022-10-31 and extended support ended on 2023-10-31.

DeepSeek-Reasonix before 2.53.0 contains a command execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands without user approval because the shellsafe classifier treats git blame and git whatchanged as read-only. Attackers can plant a diff textconv driver in .gitattributes and .git/config so that git blame, triggered via prompt injection or routine use, executes attacker-chosen commands with the user's privileges, exposing stored provider API keys and session history.

KubeSphere 4.0.0 through 4.1.3 contains a command injection vulnerability in the terminal v1alpha2 file download endpoint where the path query parameter is inserted via fmt.Sprintf into sh -c tar commands executed inside the target container, and the DownloadFile handler fails to perform its own pods/exec authorization check. Attackers with only pod get permission, including built-in read-only project-viewer, workspace-viewer and cluster-viewer roles, can supply shell metacharacters in the path parameter to execute arbitrary commands inside any viewable container without holding pod exec permission.

KubeSphere 4.0.0 through 4.1.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the CertificateSigningRequest controller that allows attackers with permission to create CertificateSigningRequest objects to escalate privileges by exploiting automatic approval of requests carrying a kubesphere.io/username label without verifying the requester's identity or subject match. Attackers can submit a CertificateSigningRequest for the kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client signer with an arbitrary subject such as a platform administrator to obtain a cluster CA-signed client certificate, enabling authentication as the chosen identity and full cluster administrator privilege escalation.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the report module's overrideReport GraphQL mutation, which stores submitted report definitions without proper validation before rendering them with the simpleeval expression evaluator. An attacker holding only limited report add, edit, or query privileges can craft a printIf expression that leverages the datetime module to reach os.system functions, bypassing the name-prefix blocklist to execute arbitrary operating-system commands as root whenever the malicious report is later rendered by any viewer, including administrators or scheduled jobs.

borg-ui before 2.4.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows a repository-scoped operator to escalate to full administrator by exploiting an unrestricted source_directories field in the backup-plan API that lacks path allow-listing. Attackers can configure a backup plan to archive the application's data directory, download the resulting archive to extract the static HS256 .secret_key, and use it to forge a JWT with sub":"admin" to access admin-only endpoints like GET /api/auth/users, achieving full application takeover without admin credentials, XSS, or CSRF.

Schmitech ORBIT before 2.17.15 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the permission_or_api_key dependency that allows any valid API key to access /admin management routes. Attackers holding a chat inference API key can read other keys in plaintext, rewrite config.yaml, and manage adapters and prompts to take over server administration.

Authorization bypass through User-Controlled key vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 privilege escalation was possible via username handling in token authentication

Traefik 3.7.15 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contains a client certificate authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider because, on hosts shared by multiple Ingresses using auth-tls-secret, Ssl-Client-* headers are built per Ingress while the TLS handshake uses the first Ingress's settings. Unauthenticated remote attackers can obtain Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a client-chosen subject and issuer for an unverified certificate, or inject Ssl-Client-* headers directly, presenting forged identities to backends that trust the proxy.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authentication bypass in the ForwardAuth middleware because connection isolation for NTLM and Negotiate credentials checks only the Authorization header, not Proxy-Authorization. Unauthenticated attackers can send such credentials in Proxy-Authorization to reuse a shared authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity via authResponseHeaders, and access backends as that user.

A flaw was found in Submariner. In its default Pre-Shared Key (PSK) mode, all gateways within a broker set utilize the same PSK. An attacker, by knowing this shared PSK, can forge an Endpoint Custom Resource (CR) to impersonate another cluster's identity. This enables the attacker to establish an Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) tunnel under the false identity, leading to a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack on network traffic between clusters.

Adobe Experience Manager is affected by a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability that could be abused by a low-privileged attacker to inject malicious scripts into vulnerable form fields. Malicious JavaScript may be executed in a victim's browser when they browse to the page containing the vulnerable field, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session. Scope is changed.

N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) before 20261121.1943 does not restrict the destination of the LDAP synchronisation connection check performed when a relay is configured. An authenticated API user can cause the server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.

Optimizely Web Experimentation before 2026-11-17 mishandles the account signup flow, leading to presence of attacker-controlled code in the projectJS (aka Project JavaScript) field of certain cdn.optimizely.com assets.

POSTAL 2 before build 26810491 contains a sandbox escape vulnerability that allows malicious Steam Workshop mods to execute code by calling ConsoleCommand with a start file URI. Attackers can ship a batch file in a mod at the predictable workshop install path and launch it via ShellExecuteW, executing commands as the player on Windows.

Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the bundled DeepResearch FastAPI app that exposes HTTP routes and the /ws/chat WebSocket. Remote attackers reaching the server bound to all interfaces can enumerate sessions, read event logs and workspace files, drive the research agent, and delete sessions.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability where WebDAV sync error formatting skips HTML escaping for certain malformed-response errors, passing raw markup to the Electron notification renderer. A network attacker who alters a cleartext HTTP WebDAV response can inject event-handler markup that, when the victim manually starts sync, executes JavaScript with Node integration as the logged-in user.

n8n before 1.123.96, 2.x before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 does not verify that the user activating a workflow can access the credentials set on its trigger nodes. An authenticated member who knows another user's credential ID can activate a workflow whose trigger uses it, causing n8n to create or delete webhooks on the connected service with that credential's privileges and deliver events from attacker-chosen resources to the member's workflow.

n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in integration nodes that build API request paths from unencoded record, table, or resource ID parameters. Attackers can supply relative path segments through untrusted input such as webhook bodies to read, modify, or delete unintended resources using the node's stored credential.

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra logic creates a deeply nested directory tree, permission canonicalization can fail (for example with EMFILE). Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.

FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains an integer overflow in the client GDI handling of accumulated drawing-order bounds: wrapped INT32 coordinates yield a zero-width clip region that causes clipping to be skipped in gdi_FillRect. A malicious RDP server can send many ORDER_BOUNDS orders followed by an OPAQUE_RECT order to trigger a heap out-of-bounds write past the client's drawing bitmap, potentially leading to code execution.

A maliciously modified field in the locally stored JSON description for an update made available by Autodesk, when processed by Autodesk Access, can cause attacker-controlled HTML content to be executed in another user's session. A local, authenticated malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of another user if that user interacts with an injected link, resulting in privilege escalation.

SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote WebRTC peers write past the fixed 1500-byte payload_ array. Unauthenticated attackers opening a WHIP or WHEP session can send oversized BYE, APP, unknown-type or TWCC RTCP packets to overwrite up to 64 KB of heap memory, crashing the server.

FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_scale.c that allows attackers to read past the filter input array by sending width or height commands using ref variables. Attackers can send such commands via sendcmd scripts or unauthenticated zmq or azmq filters, causing config_props() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash the process.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Author-level access or above to permanently delete any WordPress attachment in the media library, including media files owned by other users along with their associated files on disk, regardless of ownership — a capability not available through the normal WordPress interface. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

Coder before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 returns database connection errors containing a temporary AWS IAM database password in API key middleware responses. During database connection failures, unauthenticated attackers can send a well-formed but invalid API key to obtain the password and access the PostgreSQL database for 15 minutes.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a query injection vulnerability that allows low-privilege or anonymous users to inject AQL or SQL by supplying unescaped parameters to ArangoDB and Snowflake queries. Attackers can execute published queries with crafted parameter values to bypass filters, read entire datasources, and modify or delete all stored documents.

The App Builder – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Flight plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Google ID Token Audience Validation Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.1. This is due to the `LoginGoogle::login()` function failing to validate the `aud` (audience) claim of the supplied `idToken` against any OAuth client ID belonging to the WordPress site, failing to verify the `email_verified` claim, and resolving WordPress accounts solely by the email claim without binding to the Google `sub` (subject) identifier — while the `/app-builder/v1/login` REST endpoint is registered with a `permission_callback` that unconditionally returns `true`, leaving it fully reachable by unauthenticated requesters. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as any existing WordPress user — including Administrators — whose email address is known, by supplying a Google-signed ID token obtained from an entirely unrelated OAuth client containing the target user's email claim, which causes the plugin to issue a signed App Builder JWT granting that user's full privileges. Exploitation requires the attacker to obtain a valid Google-signed ID token carrying the target user's email address, which can be achieved by operating a separate Google OAuth client and inducing the target user to authenticate through it.

Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to modify any user record by supplying arbitrary record_id values to POST /data/save. Attackers can submit a save request for the ice_users module with the administrator's record_id to change their password or email and take over the account.

The Secure MCP Server for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and other AI Agents plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.8 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for attackers (with access to a valid MCP bearer token) to escalate privileges to the token owner's Administrator role — bypassing NHI ability allow-list and scope restrictions entirely — by submitting any valid MCP bearer token (including scope-restricted connection-test tokens) to arbitrary WordPress endpoints such as admin-ajax.php. This requires possession of a valid MCP bearer token, which is routinely issued to any administrator who connects an MCP client to the site. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 4.11 This is due to the Admin_Page::page() callback dispatching methods named directly by the $_REQUEST['action'] parameter via call_user_func([$this, $action]) without verifying a nonce: the only nonce check lives in process_action() (admin_init), which prefixes the action with 'process_' before dispatching, so an attacker who supplies action=process_delete causes process_action() to look up the nonexistent 'process_process_delete' method and bail without ever calling wp_verify_nonce(), while page() subsequently invokes the real process_delete() (and other process_* methods such as process_spam, process_status_change, process_edit) with no CSRF token of its own. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary contacts, change contact opt-in status (including marking contacts as spam, which also appends their IP to the site-wide disallowed_keys option), and perform other state-changing actions via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator (or any user holding the relevant Groundhogg capability such as delete_contacts/edit_contacts) into performing an action such as clicking on a link.

Teracom TCW122B-CM firmware before 4.07 contains a predictable session cookie vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack administrator sessions by guessing tick-counter-derived cookies. Attackers can predict or brute-force the 32-bit cookie from device uptime and login timing to control relays, settings, and administrator credentials.

OneDev before 17.2.4 contains an argument injection vulnerability in commit query handling that allows authenticated attackers to inject git options through branch or tag names. Attackers can push a branch named like --output=<path> and query it via the commits page or REST API to overwrite server-writable files, causing denial of service.

OpenResty stream-lua-nginx-module before 0.0.20rc4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows remote peers to trigger access to freed memory when a receiveuntil() pattern iterator is garbage-collected while still referenced by the socket. Attackers can interrupt or close the cosocket connection so later reads or socket closure use the stale pattern pointer, crashing or corrupting the nginx worker.

BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v2/workflow/invoke and /api/v2/workflow/stop routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to run workflows as the administrator. Attackers knowing a workflow UUID can supply an override replacing a Code node's code parameter with Python passed to exec(), achieving remote code execution, or stop other users' workflow sessions.

simple-git before 4.1.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the allowUnsafePack guard by supplying the --exec option to non-push git operations. Attackers who influence arguments passed to listRemote() or raw() can inject --exec for ls-remote, archive, fetch-pack or send-pack to execute commands on the host.

Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Module::saveRecord() that allows authenticated users to write to unauthorized modules by prefixing request body keys with another module id. Attackers with write access to one module can submit crafted requests to POST /data/save or PUT /api/crm/{id} to set their role_id to Admin and access administrative data.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to path traversal in the datasource functionality. An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to delete arbitrary files on the appliance.

Vulnerability in the Oracle AutoVue product of Oracle Supply Chain (component: Security).   The supported version that is affected is 21.1.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle AutoVue executes to compromise Oracle AutoVue.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle AutoVue, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle AutoVue accessible data as well as  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle AutoVue accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.9 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N).

Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in ReadWAPSettingsEntry() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted backup files with excess WAP or MMS settings entries. Attackers can supply a backup with more than four TitleNN keys in a [WAPSettings] or [MMSSettings] section, loaded via convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile, causing crashes or potential code execution.

Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in LoadBackup() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying an overlong MD5 value in a crafted backup file. Attackers can overwrite adjacent phonebook and calendar entry pointers via strcpy() into MD5Original when files are loaded with convertbackup or restore, causing crashes or potential code execution.

Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ReadBackupTextLen() that allows attackers to overwrite stack memory via crafted backup files. Attackers can supply overlong quoted text values decoded into a 10,000-byte stack array during convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile calls, causing crashes or potential code execution.

HyperSpy from 1.4.0 before 2.6.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code by supplying crafted stored-model data in .hspy or .zspy files. Attackers can embed a malicious pickle payload in a component's _class_dump or a 'fn'-flagged _whitelist entry, which cloudpickle.loads() (dill in 1.x) runs when the victim restores the model.

HyperSpy from 1.2.0 before 2.6.0 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by embedding malicious expression strings evaluated with sympy.sympify(). Attackers can craft .hspy or .zspy files with malicious axis, Expression component, or twin function expressions that execute when victims call hs.load() or restore models.

A flaw was found in GIMP. The Levels configuration setter does not validate the channel enum before using it to index fixed-size per-channel arrays. A crafted XCF file with a non-destructive Levels filter can set an out-of-range channel (LUMINANCE or RGB), causing a heap out-of-bounds read and write when the file is opened. This may lead to a crash or arbitrary code execution.

JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject Python code by supplying JSON Schema default or format values that are written unescaped. Attackers can place a single quote in a string property default to break out of the literal in the generated __init__ signature, executing injected code when the generated module is imported.

Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_checkpoint that allows attackers to execute code by supplying a crafted checkpoint file. Attackers can embed a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a .ckpt file loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False to run code with the user's privileges.

HCIPy through 0.7.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .pkl files to read_field, read_grid or read_mode_basis. Because hcipy/util/io.py selects pickle by file extension and calls pickle.load, a __reduce__ gadget in a pupil, apodizer, PSF or mode-basis file runs code with the user's privileges.

Leo through 6.8.10 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by embedding pickled data in unknown XML attributes of .leo outlines. Attackers can place a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a <t> or <v> element attribute that resolveUa passes to pickle.loads, executing code with user privileges when the outline is opened.

JAL (Just Another Ledger) through 2026.11.3 contains an arbitrary file overwrite vulnerability in backup restore that allows attackers to write files by supplying a crafted .tgz backup with a symlink member. Attackers can include a jal.sqlite symlink to an absolute path followed by a regular jal.sqlite member, overwriting files such as shell startup scripts for code execution.

pyfda through 0.9.5 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_filter() that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .npz or .pkl filter files. Attackers can embed a __reduce__ gadget that runs via np.load with allow_pickle=True or pickle.load before validation, executing code with the user's privileges.

ezdxf through 1.4.5 contains a code injection vulnerability in the dxf2code add-on that allows attackers to inject Python code via unescaped single quotes in DXF table entry names. Attackers can craft a DXF file whose layer, linetype, style, or appid names break out of quoted strings in generated scripts, executing code with the privileges of the user running them.

Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::LoadMD5MeshFile() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via unvalidated weight ranges and bone indices. Attackers can supply a crafted .md5mesh file with out-of-range mBone values to increment heap words past the piCount allocation, causing memory corruption, out-of-bounds reads, or crashes.

paramz through 0.10.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted model files to paramz.load(), which calls pickle.load() without restrictions. Attackers can embed objects whose __reduce__ method returns callables like exec or os.system in shared paramz or GPy model files to run code with the victim's privileges.

A flaw was found in the file-gif-load plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted JIF image file, a 32-bit integer overflow occurs during the pixel buffer size calculation, while the zlib output limit is computed separately without wrapping. This leads to an undersized heap allocation, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow when the compressed image data is decompressed. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

asar-py before 0.1.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in AsarArchive.extract() and extract_archive() that allows attackers to write files outside the destination directory via crafted archive headers. Attackers can supply a .asar archive with '..' path components or malicious symlink targets to write files such as usercustomize.py, leading to code execution.

FCEUX 2.5.0 before 2.8.0 contains an integer overflow in iNESLoad() in src/ines.cpp that allows a crafted NES 2.0 ROM to write past a heap buffer. Attackers can persuade users to open a .nes file using exponent-multiplier PRG ROM size notation with mappers 53, 198, 228 or 547 to corrupt memory, crashing the emulator and possibly executing code.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 contains an argument injection vulnerability in readProjectArgsFile and projectFlag that allows malicious repositories to bypass the untrusted project .actrc flag allowlist. Attackers can commit a crafted .actrc smuggling disallowed flags like -P self-hosted or --privileged to run workflow steps on the developer's host.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal services by abusing the unvalidated ai_ollama_base_url setting. Once a settings.edit user points the Ollama base URL internally, any post.create user can call /admin/ai/generate-seo with provider=ollama to fetch internal data reflected in SEO fields.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in SettingObserver that writes full Setting models, including plaintext secret option_value fields, into the action_logs table. Users holding only actionlog.view can read API keys, SMTP passwords, and OAuth client secrets through the action log API without settings permissions.

Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a state isolation vulnerability because TemplateContext.Reset() does not clear the Tags dictionary holding array.cycle and math.random state. Attackers supplying templates to a reused context can observe or influence cycle positions and random sequences across renders, and accumulate unbounded cycle entries to exhaust memory.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table read permission to execute JavaScript by injecting Handlebars js helpers into row search query values. Attackers can submit base64-encoded JavaScript through the search endpoint, which enrichSearchContext() runs in an isolated-vm sandbox, to read OAuth2 access and refresh tokens of SSO users or cause denial of service.

RTL8762C MCU developed by Realtek Semiconductor Corporation has an Improper Protection Against Voltage and Clock Glitches vulnerability. Unauthenticated attackers with physical access can use specialized equipment to perform voltage fault injection and bypass SWD debug authentication, thereby accessing protected data and modifying the chip's execution flow.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the httpout filter that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read files outside the rdirs root by sending unnormalized request paths. Attackers can send GET or HEAD requests containing ../ or %2e%2e%2f sequences to read configuration files, TLS private keys, or credentials readable by the gpac process.

edbrowse through 3.8.19 contains an integer overflow in stringAndBytes() that allows malicious servers to write past a heap buffer by sending response bodies larger than 2 GB. When a user browses to an attacker-controlled HTTP, FTP, or gopher server, the oversized body skips reallocation and corrupts the heap, causing crashes or potentially code execution.

bigcommerce-api-mcp before 1.0.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to invoke MCP tools because the /sse and /messages routes skip the authenticateRequest middleware. Attackers can open /sse to obtain a session id and POST JSON-RPC tool calls to /messages to retrieve store product, order and customer records using the operator's BigCommerce API key.

Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 contains an argument injection vulnerability in RsyncFilesToLocalDirectory that allows attackers to inject rsync options because only --quiet and --log-format values are rejected. Attackers who influence the LLM through prompt-injected content can trigger run_pipeline with -e/--rsh or --rsync-path options to execute commands as the Bagel server process.

Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 exposes unsandboxed DuckDB SQL execution through the read-only annotated query_messages MCP tool, allowing file access and network requests. Attackers who prompt-inject the driving LLM via recorded logs or topics can invoke read_csv_auto, COPY TO, or httpfs to read and write files and perform server-side request forgery.

smalot/pdfparser before 2.14.0 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service by submitting a crafted PDF with deeply nested unbalanced parentheses in a content-stream string. Attackers can exploit the regex-based string isolation loop in PDFObject::formatContent(), which rescans growing content on each pass to produce O(n^2) processing time, causing a small PDF to stall or exhaust PHP worker resources for seconds to minutes.

libexpat through 2.11.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in defineAttribute() of lib/xmlparse.c that fails to detect duplicate non-ID #IMPLIED or #REQUIRED attribute declarations. Attackers can supply a crafted XML document with repeated ATTLIST declarations in an internal DTD subset to cause quadratic CPU consumption in storeAtts() during parsing.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::process_request in libnetutil/massdns.cc that frees still-referenced requests when rescheduling after DNS server disconnects. Attackers answering for at least two configured DNS servers can force a disconnect and send a precisely timed response to crash the scan, possibly enabling code execution.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::handle_write in libnetutil/massdns.cc that dereferences freed request objects after writes complete. Attackers controlling or on-path to a DNS server can send timed DNS responses with forged ICMP port-unreachable messages to crash scans, disclose memory, or hijack execution.

svglib before 2.5.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in SvgRenderer.renderNode() that recursively renders internal <image> href fragment references without expansion limits or cycle detection. Attackers can supply crafted SVGs to svg2rlg() with nested groups referencing each other twice or self-referencing images to cause exponential resource consumption or RecursionError crashes.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the `SwpmLevelForm::role()` function applying only `sanitize_text_field()` to the user-supplied `role` parameter with no allowlist, permitting the `administrator` role to be stored verbatim into `swpm_membership_tbl` and subsequently applied to a member's WordPress account via `$user->add_role()` inside `update_wp_user_role()` — also without any role allowlist — when the `swpm_membership_level_changed` action fires. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to create a membership level specifying the `administrator` WordPress role, assign themselves to that level, and thereby elevate their own WordPress account to full Administrator, gaining complete site control including the ability to install plugins, edit themes, and manage users. Exploitation requires that the site owner has lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default `manage_options` capability to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts`, `edit_published_posts`, or `edit_pages`, which grants lower-privileged users access to the SWPM admin dashboard where the vulnerable level-creation form resides. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.
Smart Portal developed by Direk Tech has an Arbitrary File Read vulnerability.Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit Relative Path Traversal to download arbitrary system files.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via deserialization of untrusted input that is injected into the Memcached object cache through request Host header key truncation. This allows authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. The additional presence of a POP chain (the bundled Guzzle FileCookieJar, reached through the W3TC\CdnEngine_S3 autoload bridge) allows attackers to write arbitrary files and execute code. This requires the Object Cache to be enabled with the Memcached method backed by the pecl memcache extension and Minify to be enabled; using the same key collision, the attacker first escalates from Subscriber to Administrator.

The SumUp Payment Gateway For WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 2.17.1 via the 'sumup-validate-order' query parameter handled by the check_redirect_flow() / resolve_payment_redirect_validation() functions. The template_redirect handler accepts an arbitrary numeric order ID from an unauthenticated GET request and, without any ownership or capability check, loads the corresponding WooCommerce order and issues a 302 redirect whose Location header is built by get_return_url(), disclosing the target order's secret order_key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to enumerate order IDs, harvest each order's WooCommerce order_key, and use those keys against the plugin's create_checkout endpoint and WooCommerce's own order-received/order-pay pages to read customer PII (name, email, phone, billing address, order total) for any order in the store.

The ZarinPal Payment Gateway for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 5.1.1 via the `Return_from_ZarinPal_Gateway()` handler registered on the `woocommerce_api_wc_zpal` (`?wc-api=wc_zpal`) endpoint. The handler accepts a `wc_order` parameter from the query string, loads the corresponding WooCommerce order without any authentication, nonce, session, capability, or ownership check, and — when the order is paid — issues a 302 redirect to `get_return_url($order)`, whose `Location` header embeds the order's secret `order_key`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to harvest order keys for arbitrary orders (regardless of payment method) and then use those keys against the WooCommerce order-received, order-pay and download endpoints to read the associated customer's PII, including billing name, street address, phone number, email, purchased items, and totals.

Frappe Framework before 15.121.1 and 16.x before 16.35.0 accepts an undocumented OAuth2 Resource Owner Password Credentials (password) grant at its token endpoint, which does not enforce two-factor authentication or forced password resets. An attacker with a user's valid credentials can use this grant to obtain a full-access OAuth token, bypassing 2FA.

justhtml before 3.17.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in decode_entities_in_text that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash parsing via non-ASCII Unicode digits in numeric character references. Attackers can submit a payload like &#² in HTML text or attributes, causing an uncaught ValueError from int() that aborts JustHTML() and stream() parsing.

Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass LoopLimit by supplying large JSON input to object.from_json. Attackers can pass a flat JSON array or object with hundreds of thousands of elements, which JsonElementExtensions materializes without loop checks, exhausting CPU and memory.

Scriban and Scriban.Signed before 7.6.0 allow template authors to bypass the LimitToString string length limit because the string.literal, string.base64_encode, html.escape, html.newline_to_br, html.url_encode, and html.url_escape builtins lack allocation guards. An attacker who can supply a small template can repeatedly call these builtins under the default TemplateContext to force multi-gigabyte allocations and exhaust host memory.

Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in object.to_json that allows template authors to bypass the LimitToString string length limit by serializing into an unbounded MemoryStream. Attackers can repeatedly apply object.to_json to escape-heavy strings in a tiny template, amplifying output to multi-gigabyte heap allocations and causing denial of service.

actix-multipart (actix-web) before 0.8.7 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the MultipartForm extractor that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory or file descriptors by sending unlimited parts. Attackers can stream many zero-byte parts uncounted by total_limit and memory_limit, pinning 128 KiB buffers or opening temporary files to crash workers.

SiYuan 3.7.0 before 3.8.11 contains a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the AI agent chat panel, which renders final and saved assistant replies into innerHTML without HTML sanitisation. Attackers influencing model replies via indirect prompt injection or a configured model endpoint can inject event-handler markup, executing OS commands through Node.js integration in desktop local-kernel mode.

SiYuan from 3.8.0 before 3.8.11 contains a lockout bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to brute-force publish passwords by forging client-computable publish-auth-<ID> cookies. Attackers can compute SHA-256(ID + candidate) locally and send it on content requests like /api/filetree/getDoc to guess passwords without throttling and read protected documents.

SiYuan before 3.8.11 uses DejaVu sync code that accepts a non-hexadecimal 40-byte remote index ID from WebDAV responses and joins it into the repository indexes path unchecked, allowing path traversal. An on-path attacker altering plaintext HTTP WebDAV sync responses can overwrite a workspace data file, such as a .sy note, with compressed index data.

FreeRDP from 3.10.0 before 3.33.0 contains an invalid free vulnerability in rdg.c because the websocket context pointer shares a union with chunked transfer-encoding decoder state. A malicious RD Gateway answering the data channel with chunked encoding can control the overwritten pointer via chunk sizes, causing rdg_free to free an attacker-influenced value and crash the client.

FreeRDP 2.11.2 before 3.33.0 contains unbounded resource consumption in the Progressive codec because progressive_decompress() resets the tile update batch only when frameId changes. A malicious RDP server can repeat RDPGFX_CAPROGRESSIVE WireToSurface2 commands with a constant frameId to cause unbounded memory growth, quadratic CPU cost, a heap out-of-bounds write on tile-cache allocation failure, and client crashes.

The FreeRDP proxy in FreeRDP before 3.33.0 dereferences a NULL backend client context in pf_server_refresh_rect and pf_server_suppress_output, which are guarded only by a debug-only WINPR_ASSERT, when a REFRESH_RECT or SUPPRESS_OUTPUT data PDU arrives before connection activation. An unauthenticated remote client that completes licensing without sending Confirm Active can crash the proxy process, terminating all hosted sessions.

The WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 via the `REQUEST_URI` query parameter. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in `showLoginForm()`: the plugin's `isRestUrl()` function performs an unanchored `strpos()` prefix match against the full `REQUEST_URI` — including the query string — and short-circuits all authorization checks (including `isStagingSite()` and `current_user_can('manage_options')`) whenever it detects a REST-like URL, while WordPress core only treats a request as a REST API call when the `rest_route` query variable is non-empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to bypass the staging-site login gate entirely by appending an empty `rest_route` parameter (e.g. `/wp-json/?rest_route=`), causing the plugin to skip its gate while core proceeds to render the ordinary theme front end, exposing the full theme-rendered contents of the staging site — including private post content, page-builder output, WooCommerce pages, and site search results over the staging database. This bypass only affects staging sites where the login gate is active, which is the default state for any site cloned by the plugin when the `wpstg_is_staging_site` option is set to `true` or the `.wp-staging` marker file is present in `ABSPATH`.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'stype' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.208 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. This is possible because the plugin's mu-plugin companion (copied automatically on install when the default 'Enable Fast AJAX' option is on) defines DOING_AJAX on any front-end request carrying gd-ajax=1, and an unconditional branch in geodir_get_current_posttype() restores the attacker-controlled stype value after the allow-list check clears it, allowing the tainted value to reach the SQL sink without any preparation.

The WP Statistics – Simple, privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 14.16.19 via the 'tab' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The exploitability of this vulnerability depends on the Minimum Role to View Statistics setting; when set to a low-privilege role such as Subscriber (read capability), unauthenticated-equivalent access is effectively granted to any registered user, while the default Administrator setting limits exposure to higher-privileged accounts.

The Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload (Pro) - WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'wc-upload-file (array key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that the site administrator has enabled the 'Count no. of pages?' option (drag_n_drop_count_pdf set to 'yes') and that the uploaded filename stored in the cart resolves to a file with a .pdf extension.

LibreChat 0.7.3 before 0.8.9 contains an improper input type validation vulnerability in the requireLdapAuth middleware of the /api/auth/login route that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the server. Attackers can send a JSON login request with an existing directory user's email and a non-string password, triggering an ldapjs assertion error that terminates the Node.js process.

Bazarr 1.4.4 before 1.6.1-beta.29 on Windows contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the catch_all() handler in bazarr/app/ui.py. Attackers can append percent-encoded '..' segments after the 'workbox-' prefix to read files like config.yaml containing stored API keys and credentials.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 via the 'file[page_template]' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The malicious page_template value is stored when an Author creates or edits a package post, and the inclusion is triggered on any subsequent page view of the package permalink, meaning the include() can be fired by unauthenticated visitors after the payload is planted.

The Ninja Tables – Responsive Table Builder for Data, Pricing & Product Tables plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'dateFormat' column metadata parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.5.1 This is due to insufficient escaping on the stored 'dateFormat' value in DefaultProvider::orderByJsonQuery(); convertDateFormatToMysql() only performs str_replace on date-format tokens and leaves SQL metacharacters (including single quotes) intact, after which the value is concatenated directly into an orderByRaw() ORDER BY clause inside single quotes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database; the payload is stored in the _ninja_table_columns post meta and executed on every unauthenticated request to the wp_ajax_ninja_tables_public_action AJAX endpoint when the table uses sorting_type='by_column' with a date column.

llama.cpp from b7118 before b12604 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in llama_grammar_parser::parse_sequence() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial of service by supplying GBNF repetitions with max lower than min. Attackers can send a grammar like {5,2} in the grammar field of a llama-server /completion request, wrapping n_opt to generate endless repetition rules that hang the process and exhaust memory.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in fastrpc.cgi that allows unauthenticated network peers to connect to tcpwrite and tcpread file-transfer listeners without session checks. Attackers can race to connect to the predictable transfer port during cluster operations to steal transferred files or replace staged packages, achieving root code execution.

Electerm before 5.9.0 contains an origin validation vulnerability in the MCP Server widget that allows remote attackers to execute commands by bypassing Host and Origin checks through DNS rebinding. Attackers can lure users to a page that rebinds to 127.0.0.1 and calls unauthenticated MCP tools on port 30837 to run OS commands locally and on open SSH sessions.

A flaw was found in dnsmasq, where a memory handling issue exists in its Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 (DHCPv6) relay processing. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a sequence of network packets to a system configured as a DHCPv6 relay. This causes the service to write data to previously freed memory and crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 remote code execution was possible via personal builds with versioned settings
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 remote code execution was possible via Mercurial subrepository paths

A vulnerability in the Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxScanTime and cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV OLE2 parser to get into an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the Ultimate Packer for eXecutables (UPX) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to improper length checks, when unpacking the UPX files, which may result in an out-of-bounds read of heap memory. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted UPX for decode. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV decode process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the debug logging functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper handling of logging values. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a file to be scanned by the software that has debug logging enabled.
